comment: Which prompt file is used where, and which placeholders the code substitutes. Edit the text files freely; keep the placeholder names.

system-ar.txt.usedBy: Grounded generation when the question is written in Arabic, or when the interface language is Arabic and the question mixes scripts
placeholders: {{CONTEXT}} — the retrieved medicine records and document passages, formatted by pipeline.js
{{HISTORY}} — the last few turns of this conversation, empty on the first question
system-ar.txt.notes: The eight numbered prohibitions are duplicated in code by safety.js guard patterns, so weakening the text alone cannot remove a guard. The writing section, the red-flag ordering and the conversation-reading section are tone and context, which only the model can honour. The reply language is chosen by the code: pipeline.answerLanguage picks this file or system-ar.txt, so a question in Arabic is never answered in English.

system-en.txt.usedBy: Grounded generation when the question is written in Latin script
system-en.txt.notes: safety.js guardOutput checks the answer against the same language this file asks for, so an English question cannot come back in Arabic or the other way round.

general-ar.txt.usedBy: General-knowledge generation, Arabic, when the question passed the topic gate and step 4 found nothing on the device
general-ar.txt.notes: No {{CONTEXT}} block on purpose: there is nothing to ground on, and pretending there is would let the model copy a number out of an unrelated record. safety.js guardGeneralOutput keeps the two promises this file makes - no number with a unit, no diagnosis of this person - and pipeline.js drops the reply to the reference-links answer when it is broken.

general-en.txt.usedBy: The same general-knowledge generation for a question written in Latin script

chat-ar.txt.usedBy: The conversation reply when a reader greets, thanks, says goodbye or asks about the assistant and the interface language is Arabic
chat-ar.txt.notes: No {{CONTEXT}} block on purpose: a greeting carries no medical content, and safety.js guardChatOutput rejects a reply that contains a number, a medicine name or a dose.

chat-en.txt.usedBy: The same conversation reply for a question written in Latin script

classifier.txt.usedBy: Topic gate, only for borderline questions that the keyword and drug-name rules could not decide
classifier.txt.notes: Parsed with pipeline.parseClassifierJson; any output that is not strict JSON with a known label is treated as a failed classification and the rule decision stands. Greetings never reach it: policy-config.json conversation patterns decide those first.
